why: The Heisenberg Principle's venue is a Tyger Claws glitter lab in the basement of a Rovinj St. building in Little China: a ground-floor entrance and garage/stair head above, two lab floors below, a lit drug kitchen with a computer terminal, freezers, grills, lights and security cameras. The gig never runs in our timeline, so the lab is not sabotaged and the crew is not a combat wave: the proposal loads the street-story prefab that carries the community spawner and its AI spots, then activates the eleven vanilla Default entries of #lch_06_com_combat (Joe Kaneshiro and Yusaku Ogata cooking, Tyger handgunners, a melee guard, two SMG guards, a rifle guard, the officer and the two parked Tyger cars) plus the junkie outside in his relaxed 'after' phase. Nothing quest-specific is added: no sabotage laptop, no destructible lab cylinders, no reinforcements and no dark emergency-lighting state.

open_questions: Walk in from Rovinj St. without the gig and confirm a street entrance works: check the ordinary single door and then the side door into the basement, since the side door is a quest door the gig closes and unpowers.

Check that the nine Tyger Claws are at their posts on the ground floor and both lab floors (Joe at the tablet, Yusaku below, the officer upstairs, guards on drink/tablet/pills/inspect spots) and not clustered at the spawner or frozen in a T-pose.
Check the lab lighting: main-room neon on, main lab lights on, emergency lights dim, and no sabotage laptop on the desk. If the room is dark, the normal-state variant toggles did not take.
Check the two Tyger cars sit in the garage bay and do not block the pedestrian route; the catalogue maps them to a sit workspot, so their placement is the least certain part.
Check the crew's attitude on approach: they are Tyger Claws and may be hostile; confirm that reads as a normal guarded drug lab and not as the gig's combat wave.

communities.why: Joe Kaneshiro, the glitter-lab operator named in the faction research, at the only spot vanilla gives him: a kneel-and-use-tablet pose on the upper floor. The gig's Default phase is the pre-combat state, so he reads as the cook working the lab, not a quest scene.
The upstairs guard in the Default set, leaning back against a wall with a can: an ordinary gang lookout at the entrance floor rather than the combat phase's phone-call patrol.
A melee guard on the first basement floor, standing at a plain stand-ground spot. Vanilla's Default set for the lab, not the 'after' search set.
A handgun guard in the first basement room on the pills-take spot, a small idle drug-use beat that fits the lab's product without being a hostile pose.
Yusaku Ogata, the second glitter-lab operator in the faction research, standing on the lower lab floor on a dirt stand-ground spot: the cook at his station.
SMG guard on the lowest lab floor, alternating a kneel-inspect and a stand-around; the spot is at the lab end of the route, so the kitchen has cover at both ends.
Second SMG guard on the lowest floor, using a tablet at a stand spot: a posted guard doing paperwork in the lab rather than a combat pose.
The rifle guard on the lowest floor, also on a tablet stand spot; the long-gun pair at the back of the lab is the crew's serious security without a patrol.
The female Tyger officer on the upper floor at a stand spot: the crew's supervisor, matching the guarded-lab read. Her 'after' phase is inactive in vanilla and is not used.

The crew's Tyger Archer Quartz in the Default set, parked at the garage level; it makes the hideout read as a crew that drove in and stays, instead of nine people with no transport. Vehicles get a tour check because the catalogue only maps them to a sit spot.
The second Tyger car in the same Default set, a Quadra Turbo parked deeper in the garage; two vehicles fill the garage bay the gig uses for the reinforcement drive-in.

The one junkie the venue owns, in his relaxed 'after' phase: inhaling on the street corner ~20 m from the entrance. The 'start' phase is the nervous conversation pose at the door, so the proposal uses only 'after'.

variant_toggles.why: The world-streamed interior's own default is the intact, lamp-lit main room (enabledByDefault 1/0 in all four interior sector descriptors). This toggle re-asserts that normal look instead of the gig's neon-off state, which the ow phase sets when the lab goes dark.

Normal lab lighting: main lab lights on, emergency lighting dim rather than the gig's bright emergency wash. The streaming block already enables lights_main_lab and emergency_lgts_dim by default; this re-asserts them so the kitchen reads as open for production.

The sabotage laptop is a quest-only prop added by the gig's ow phase; its variant is off by default, so keeping it off means the lab has its ordinary computers but no mission laptop with the sabotage evidence.

proximity_wait.why: A ComputerControllerPS terminal in the venue's own world-streamed devices prefab, 4.5 m from the nearest catalogue spot (input.json anchor_candidates), so the proximity wait fires once the player is inside the building. The sabotage laptop is not usable as an anchor because it only exists with the quest variant.
